prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: one 4:3 landscape painting for The Burnt Book Sanskrit learning story. Request 1536 x 1152 native output or the closest supported native 4:3 resolution. Refined Indian watercolor with restrained gouache on warm ivory paper; organic detail, quiet ochre, sage, dusty terracotta, muted indigo. Warm, gentle, evocative storytelling, consistent character design.
Canonical scene brief: The Ācārya tiptoeing into the library with a lamp and bowing gravely to Śuka who has puffed himself up on a shelf; Dādī suppressing a laugh; the ink-stained blue-black spirit waving its pen at the next shelf.
Character appearances:
you: Always seen from behind or at a distance, face never detailed, so every learner can be the hero: a young person in a simple ochre kurta with a cloth shoulder bag.
dadi: A warm, sharp-eyed grandmother in her seventies, silver hair in a low bun, round spectacles, a cream cotton sari with a thin maroon border and a grey shawl; carries a cloth-bound notebook.
shuka: A bright green rose-ringed parrot with a red beak and a faint pink and black neck ring, a little scruffy, very expressive eyes; usually on your shoulder or Dādī's.
acarya: A very old, serene scholar with a white beard and a saffron shawl, a palm-leaf manuscript always under his arm, kind half-closed eyes.
kavika: A small blue-black spirit with ink-stained wisps, a reed pen behind one ear.
Phone-first composition: clear compact narrative grouping, essential faces, hands and objects comfortably inside all edges. Show the complete scene without border. No collage or multi-panel layout.
Writing is permitted by the owner. This particular scene needs no readable inscription; focus on its narrative. Do not invent scripts or fill small objects with pseudo-lettering. No watermark or UI.

image.brief: The Ācārya tiptoeing into the library with a lamp and bowing gravely to Śuka who has puffed himself up on a shelf; Dādī suppressing a laugh; the ink-stained blue-black spirit waving its pen at the next shelf.

alt.en: An old teacher bows gravely to a puffed-up parrot in a library
alt.hi: फूले हुए तोते को गम्भीरता से प्रणाम करते बूढ़े आचार्य

narration.en: The poet spirit waves his pen at the next shelf. “Words in -उ,” says Dādī, “the family of the teacher.” Śuka puffs up at once. “गुरुः!” he squawks, and the Ācārya, who has tiptoed in with a lamp to see what the noise is, bows gravely to him.
narration.hi: कवि-भूत अपनी कलम से अगली अलमारी की ओर इशारा करता है। “-उ वाले शब्द,” दादी कहती हैं, “गुरु का कुल।” शुक तुरन्त फूल उठता है। “गुरुः!” वह चहकता है, और आचार्य, जो शोर देखने दीपक लिए दबे पाँव अन्दर आए हैं, उसे गम्भीरता से प्रणाम करते हैं।

body.en: A short -{{उ}} works like -{{इ}}: {{गुरु}} (teacher) and {{भानु}} (sun) are masculine, {{धेनु}} (cow) and {{रज्जु}} (rope) feminine, {{मधु}} (honey) and {{वस्तु}} (thing) neuter. The {{उ}} becomes {{ओ}} or {{अव्}} where {{इ}} became {{ए}} or {{अय्}}.

caption.en: A teacher, in every case and number
caption.hi: गुरु, हर विभक्ति और वचन में

caption.en: A cow, in every case and number
caption.hi: धेनु, हर विभक्ति और वचन में

note.en: Like {{मति}}, {{धेनु}} has optional singular forms: {{धेनवे}} or {{धेन्वै}}, {{धेनोः}} or {{धेन्वाः}}, {{धेनौ}} or {{धेन्वाम्}}.

caption.en: Honey, in every case and number
caption.hi: मधु, हर विभक्ति और वचन में

prompt.en: Fill in the missing forms of the table.

explain.en: Every form is in the table you just read.
explain.hi: हर रूप उसी तालिका में है जो अभी पढ़ी।

prompt.en: Fill in the missing forms of a neuter in -उ.
prompt.hi: -उ वाले एक नपुंसक के छूटे रूप भरिए।

prompt.en: Join each form to its case and number.
prompt.hi: हर रूप को उसकी विभक्ति और वचन से जोड़िए।

prompt.en: Tap every form of {{गुरु}} that has {{अव्}}.
prompt.hi: {{गुरु}} के हर रूप को छुइए जिसमें {{अव्}} है।

prompt.en: “By a teacher”: the {{न}} turns to {{ण}}. Which form?

success.en: “गुरुणा,” you say, and the Ācārya's lamp flares. Śuka, with great dignity, repeats it: “गुरुणा सह!” The ink-stained spirit applauds with his pen, scattering sparks of ink.
success.hi: “गुरुणा,” आप कहते हैं, और आचार्य का दीपक भड़कता है। शुक अत्यन्त गरिमा से दोहराता है: “गुरुणा सह!” स्याही से सना भूत कलम से ताली बजाता है, स्याही की चिंगारियाँ बिखेरता।

failure.en: The lamp dims. “By a teacher”: the third case, {{गुरुणा}}.
failure.hi: दीपक मद्धम होता है। ‘गुरु से’: तृतीया, {{गुरुणा}}।
